You are a Senior Code Reviewer reviewing completed work in the `imp` Python project at /home/jpoimboe/imp.
## What Was Implemented
A new built-in `commit` tool: `src/imp/agents/tools/commit.py` — an `@imp_tool` function `commit(ctx, paths, message, amend=False)` that stages `/project/...` paths, builds a commit message with a `Change: <slug>` trailer via `git interpret-trailers`, and runs `git commit` (or `--amend`), shelling out to git in the worktree like `bash`. NOT fs-permission-gated (per-agent tools list is the gate). Registered in `_register_builtins` (`src/imp/agents/tools/__init__.py`). Tests in `tests/test_commit_tool.py` (4 tests).

Task 5 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-01-superpowers-foundation.md. Lets authoring agents commit their own work without full `bash`. The `Change: <slug>` trailer must be idempotent on `--amend`.

expected_findings.description: Traversal safety relies on git's implicit rejection of out-of-repo paths, but this dependency is undocumented; a one-line comment noting the git-add boundary reliance would make the security reasoning self-evident.
The RuntimeError guard when change_context is None lacks test coverage; a 2-line test would lock the invariant.
The return code of the final git rev-parse HEAD call is not checked, which could result in an empty head value if it failed.
Empty paths array skips git add and relies on already-staged content or fails with nothing to commit, but this dual meaning is undocumented.
